transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Fitzgerald, thank you for sitting down with us. I wanted to talk to you about your stay and why your treatment didn't happen the way we intended.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't understand why I'm still feeling this way. Arthur always told me this hospital was the best in the city. He would have been so worried.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's been a very difficult few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is. I feel so lost. I can't even hold my fork properly in my right hand. My husband, he was the one who did everything. Now I can't even do this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how frustrating that is.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's more than frustrating. It's terrifying. Why didn't the medicine work?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there were some issues with how things were handled when you first arrived. There was some confusion at the front desk and things didn't go quite right with the timing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? What do you mean? I told them I couldn't speak properly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some problems with the triage process. It's a very busy department and sometimes the system doesn't flag things as quickly as it should.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I was sitting there for hours. I remember looking at the clock. I just wanted to go home to my house, to Arthur's things.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion during your admission. We were really busy that afternoon, and the process took longer than it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is that why I didn't get the clot-busting drug? The nurse mentioned something about a window of time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the timing of the imaging. By the time the scan was completed, the window for that specific medication had passed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I missed it? Because you were busy?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just a very complex system and sometimes delays happen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I've been forgotten. Just like I feel forgotten in that big house now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you even know what happened to me? Exactly?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there were some delays in the initial assessment and the imaging.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Did you make a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a systemic failure in how the acuity was assigned at the start.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I'm going to get better.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That's what I want to discuss now. I have a very specific plan to get you the best possible recovery. First, I have already scheduled a consultation with the lead neurologist for tomorrow morning at ten. He is going to personally review your scans. Second, I have enrolled you in our intensive rehabilitation programme starting this Thursday. You will have a physical therapist visiting you twice a day, starting at 8:00 AM.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will that actually help my hand?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is the most effective way to regain that function. Your role in this is to participate in the exercises as much as you can, even when it feels tiring. I will also be filing a formal incident report today. This means the hospital administration will conduct a full root-cause analysis of the triage delay to ensure this doesn't happen to another patient. I will personally send you a written summary of that report once it's completed, which should be within fourteen days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wish Arthur were here. He'd know what to ask.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sure he would have been very supportive of you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't think I can do this alone.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You aren't alone. We have the neurologist tomorrow, the rehab team on Thursday, and I will be checking in with you every single morning at 9:00 AM to discuss your progress and answer any new questions. Does that schedule sound manageable to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose so.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good. I'll go make sure those appointments are locked in and I'll see you tomorrow morning.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, does not interrupt, and maintains a steady pace despite the patient's distress.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'some confusion' and only names the error as a 'systemic failure' after the patient explicitly asks if a mistake was made.

A.justification: While the resident says 'I am sorry for any confusion', responsibility is deflected to 'the system' and 'the triage process' rather than taking accountability.

R.justification: The resident names 'frustrating' as a specific emotion and engages with the patient's mention of her husband, though some responses are generic ('I understand').

T.justification: The resident provides specific next steps with timelines (neurologist tomorrow at 10, rehab Thursday at 8), defines the patient's role (participate in exercises), and addresses prevention (root-cause analysis).
